item.title: Python Pillow: Understanding Image Modes L, P, and RGB
item.description:
“Python Pillow: Understanding Image Modes L, P, and RGB”

When working with images in Python using the Pillow library (a fork of PIL), you’ll frequently encounter different image modes. Understanding these modes—specifically L, P, and RGB—is crucial for efficient image manipulation and storage. Each mode has distinct characteristics impacting file size, color representation, and processing.

Image Modes Explained

RGB Mode: In RGB mode, each pixel is represented by three values: one for Red, one for Green, and one for Blue. This is the standard for full-color images. Each channel typically uses 8 bits, meaning each pixel requires 3 bytes of storage. This offers a wide spectrum of colors but can be more storage-intensive.
